slides.sub: The work they hate doing. The work they can't afford to hire for. Atris does both — inside their company, with a receipt every time.

slides.heading: One closed loop, fully receipted.
slides.sub: Context in. Member acts. Proof out. Outcome graded. Reward signal flows back. The agent is sharper next week.

slides.heading: One machine, N customers.
slides.sub: Each with their own disk, own behavior, own reward signal. Same code everywhere. No data crosses.

Mem0 stores facts. Letta stores context. Glean indexes docs. Atris is the only one where the customer's runtime ships back a reward signal so the agent gets measurably better at their work — with the data never leaving their perimeter.

slides.heading: Why now
slides.sub: The labs are becoming the new oil companies. Standard Oil didn't lose to a better well — it lost to the refinery.

columns.b: Tokens regulated. Frontier access limited. Customer-by-customer approval. The race for the smartest brain is becoming a utility.
Thin GPT wrappers are over. What's alive is the layer beneath — memory, taste, approval, proof, on the customer's perimeter.
Installation phase, pre-deployment. History says the next decade's winners are not the rail-layers. Amazon over Cisco. Google over WorldCom.

slides.sub: Memory, taste, approval, proof. Running inside the customer's perimeter. Getting sharper every week. The labs build the models. We build the seat the model sits in.

slides.text: Solo founder. Two production customers. Builds the company on the product.
slides.sub: Atris runs Atris. The weekly business review you'd run on Atris is the same one I ran to prep this pitch. The chip on the shoulder is that nobody else is willing to live inside their own product long enough to make it real.
